blocks.text: Located on the first floor of the Grand Palais, the Emergence sector brings together twenty solo projects from nine countries. It spotlights a new generation of international artists presented by emerging galleries.

The selected projects explore very different realities, from the closest everyday life to the historical and political narratives that shape our present. Ricardo Cases (Galeria Reus, Palma), for instance, photographs a carpenter napping in his workshop, in a body of work that questions time, repetition and the gestures of daily life.

Other artists address history, memory and the absence of images. Randa Mirza (Tanit, Beirut) combines photography, poetry and calligraphy to evoke the destruction caused by war in southern Lebanon and to try to grasp what is in the process of disappearing. Nicolas Combarro (NORDÉS, A Coruña), for his part, enters into dialogue with the material and immaterial remains of architecture.
With Hôtel de l’artefact spolié , Agnes Essonti Luque (Bombon Projects, Barcelona) examines colonial plunder and the restitution of objects.

Norwegian artist Dev Dhunsi (Melk, Oslo) draws on personal, diasporic and colonial narratives to examine how images, materials and spaces shape experiences of belonging, uprootedness and representation; the work creates a space where documentary and myth, archive and allegory, photography and textile intertwine.

This opening toward new material forms also runs through the works of Wysocka & Pogo and Kristina Õllek (Open Doors, London), while artists such as Brandon Gercara (DS Galerie, Paris) and Yumna Al Arashi (Homecoming, Amsterdam) move these questions into fictional territories.
Prix de la Maison Ruinart, Partner of Paris Photo’s Emergence Sector

Each year, the Prix de la Maison Ruinart honors a project presented in the Emergence sector. Maison Ruinart commissions a specific work from the selected artist, accompanied by a grant. The resulting work is then presented in a dedicated space at Paris Photo.
In 2026, the prize goes to Philippe Jarrigeon, presented by Womanray
Paris Photo Nov. 12–15, 2026 | Grand Palais 1 pm – 8 pm (Sunday 7 pm) Avenue Winston Churchill 75008, Paris, France Booth P01 www.parisphoto.com
